title: Request tracking: choose the layout
question: Three of seven layouts, dealt by the roll. The EquiFreight style stays as it is; this choice is only about how the page is organised.

options.label: Owed first
options.thesis: Opens on what the customer owes and by when, then shows where the move stands.
options.viewport: Request header and stage chip, then a full-width 'You owe' list (upload Nightfall's EIA test by 11 Oct, extend insurance), then stage track, route and history side by side.
options.risk: When the customer owes nothing, the lead area goes empty and needs a strong 'nothing needed from you' state.

options.label: Route as the page
options.lineage: one line from stable to destination
options.thesis: One continuous line: the paperwork is the stretch before the ramp, the journey is the stretch after it.
materials: schematic route line with stage nodes
clearance gate drawn as a lock on the line
options.viewport: A full-width line: request, quote, approval, documents, a locked gate, then pickup, border, welfare stop, delivery. The current node is lit; the panel below expands whichever node is selected.
options.risk: Pre-departure stages take weeks and trip legs take hours, so the line must be spaced by stage, not by time, and say so.

regions.label: Route line · before departure | gate | on the road

options.label: Next-step spine
options.lineage: vertical stage list, current stage open
options.thesis: A vertical spine of seven stages. The current one opens in place; everything else is one line.
materials: Step component scaled up to a spine
the current stage's own content inline (quote, documents, route)
options.viewport: A banner naming the next step and its owner ('You: upload 4 health certificates by 11 Oct'). Below it the spine, with done stages collapsed to a date and the current stage expanded, next to a sticky summary of horses, route, quote and key dates.
options.risk: The page gets long when the documents stage is open for four horses; it needs per-horse grouping to stay scannable.

regions.label: Summary rail · horses, route, quote, dates
